text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Gabor Kuncze, executive president of the Free Democrats, said Sunday he is convinced his party must prepare for a role in government after the 1998 elections. The party parliamentary group is expected to elect Foreign Ministry state secretary Istvan Szent-Ivanyi as its leader today.

- Young Democrats re-elected Viktor Orban as party president at their weekend national congress. The congress approved a series of tenets to be used as policy basis, stressing a coalition of moderate centre-right, middle-class forces to "create a new, modern, 21st century Hungary".

- Thirty-five conservative Christian and national-liberal parties from Central Europe founded the Central European Democratic Forum on Saturday in Lakitelek and promised to work together to overcome left-wing forces in the region.
- Christian Democrat president Gyorgy Giczy tried to distance himself Saturday from a Friday statement that the party would sever ties with the far-right Hungarian Justice and Life Party.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Croatian President Franjo Tudjman will address the House today. (Sat.)
- Agriculture Minister Frigyes Nagy stressed Friday that the government has no plans to allow foreigners to buy land in Hungary. (Sat.)
- The state privatisation agency APV posted revenues of 11.019 billion forints and spent 4.479 billion forints in the first two months of this year.
- The retail chain Skala-Coop Rt will inject one billion forints into sister retailer Centrum Aruhazak Rt., raising the latter's share capital to six billion forints.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- The information prospectus on the $300 million offering of share in the Hungarian oil and gas company MOL was completed and made public on Friday, ahead of a roadshow that starts in London and the Far East today.
- The current account deficit for January was $300 milion, the National Bank of Hungary reported on Friday.

- Work is to begin immediately on a series of measures designed to mitigate the impact of the M5 toll highway, as agreed by the Ministry of Transport and mayors of towns along the Budapest-Kecskemet road.
- The board of directors of the state privatisation agency APV on Friday approved the sale of 1.8 million shares, over 10 percent of the total, in the pharmaceutical company Richter Gedeon.

- K&H Bank approved an IAS report on its subsidiary Kvantum Investment Bank Rt., showing total assets of 3.58 billion forints, pre-tax profits of 309 million forints and balance sheet profits of 240 million forints for 1996.
- Electrical equipment trading company Transelektro posted after-tax profits of 813.5 million forints on sales of 23.2 billion forints last year, double the 1995 result.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn today becomes the first Hungarian premier to visit Malaysia, after winding up his visit to Singapore.
- The National Bank of Hungary's 1996 balance sheet shows total assets of 5,119.3 billion forints, down 5.6 percent from January 1, last year.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
